# AABB Collision Detection

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## AABB Collision Detection

Wall bouncing checks whether the ball has crossed a boundary. Detecting whether the ball has hit a brick or the paddle is a different kind of check. You need to know if two shapes are overlapping.

The technique for this is called AABB, which stands for Axis-Aligned Bounding Box. The idea is simple. Two rectangles are overlapping only when all four of these are true at the same time:

- The left edge of A is to the left of the right edge of B
- The right edge of A is to the right of the left edge of B
- The top edge of A is above the bottom edge of B
- The bottom edge of A is below the top edge of B

If any one of those is false, there is a gap between them and no collision.For the ball we treat it as a small rectangle using its center plus and minus its radius as the box edges.

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3
4const ball = { x: 190, y: 170, radius: 10 };
5const brick = { x: 150, y: 160, w: 100, h: 30 };
6
7// ball: { x, y, radius }, rect: { x, y, w, h }
8function overlaps(ball, rect) {
9  return ball.x - ball.radius < rect.x + rect.w &&
10         ball.x + ball.radius > rect.x &&
11         ball.y - ball.radius < rect.y + rect.h &&
12         ball.y + ball.radius > rect.y;
13}
14
15const hit = overlaps(ball, brick);
16
17ctx.fillStyle = hit ? "#e74c3c" : "#95a5a6";
18ctx.fillRect(brick.x, brick.y, brick.w, brick.h);
19ctx.fillStyle = "#000";
20ctx.beginPath();
21ctx.arc(ball.x, ball.y, ball.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
22
23ctx.fill();
```

Run this and the brick turns red because the ball overlaps it. Try changing ball.x to 50 and the brick turns grey - no overlap. The overlaps(ball, rect) function is a reusable collision test you can call with any ball and any brick object.

Treating a circle as a small square for AABB is a deliberate shortcut. Mathematically the corner of the bounding box is slightly outside the actual circle, so AABB can register a hit a pixel or two before the shapes visually touch. For a fast-moving ball in a game like Brick Breaker, the difference is imperceptible. Keep the collision logic in its own function so you can call it for every brick in the grid and for the paddle in a single loop.

![Two rectangles with labeled edges showing the four overlap conditions: left A less than right B, right A greater than left B, top A less than bottom B, bottom A greater than top B](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)
